transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are at the gate. That is all. The rest is not with me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I came to go beyond it and bring my brother Omar back. He was taken when I dared him to insult the well.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Names drift. Dares drift. Boys fall all the time.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He didn't mean it, and neither did I. I just need to see him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Need is thin. It passes through and leaves no mark. I am not holding anything.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not asking for treasure or mercy. I just want to reach what's past you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Past is a direction, not a permission. I do not decide it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then tell me who does, or where to stand. I can wait.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Waiting happens without you. Stones do it better.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not a stone. I'm his brother.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Brothers blur. The dark smooths them.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He used to whistle when he was nervous, even when no one was there.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Sounds linger. Then they don't. The dark has its own noise.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I hear it when I sleep, like he's afraid. I should have stopped him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Sleep is a surface habit. Fear feeds everything down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He followed me everywhere when we were small. I owe him more than this.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Owing is a word humans keep. Debts dissolve.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I can't bring him back, tell me how to remember him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Remembering is not a skill. It happens until it doesn't. I do not teach it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm afraid his face is already changing in my head. I don't want the dark to win that.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Faces change everywhere. Time does that without caves or kings. The dark is not competing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If he's still alive, I want him to know I came. Even if he never sees me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Knowing travels poorly. Messages thin out and tear. Most never arrive.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I'll stay close enough that it doesn't have far to go.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Close is a measure you brought with you. Distances here fold and forget themselves. Staying does not press the way you think.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He hated figs but ate them anyway so my mother wouldn't notice. He always wiped his hands on his shirt after.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Small refusals. They make little shapes before they fade. The dark keeps no record of shirts or fruit.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: When we argued, he'd give me his bread the next morning and not say why. That was how he said sorry.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Gestures pass through places like this. Some slow down. I am listening to how you place them.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He laughed too loud when he was scared, like he could scare it back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Loud laughter frays first. Fear learns its edges from that. You are circling him without touching.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know how to touch him from here. I only know how he sounded.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Sound is thinner than you think, but it leaves residue. You keep bringing residue instead of demands. That is different.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't have anything else. These are the pieces I carried down.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Pieces pile up. Sometimes they start to resemble weight. I have not moved, but the air has.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I stop talking about him, it feels like setting him down somewhere I can't see.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: My eyes did something just now. Where did you last set him, exactly?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: By the well's stones. He was still laughing, and his heel kept knocking the rim.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stones remember pressure longer than sound. That detail did not need to arrive here. And yet.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know why I said it. It's just where he was.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Things placed without reason tend to stay. I am not done with that image, but I will not explain it to you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You don't have to. I just needed somewhere to put it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You have been putting things down this whole time without asking if the floor would hold them. It did. That is not nothing, even here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I'll keep doing it until something opens.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Something already has. The gate is open now, and it did not need your eyes on it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm going through. I won't forget where I stood.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: What passes through keeps the shape it entered with, for a while. Do not waste that while.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't rush it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm going to find him.
